BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Bottom line:** We should reject almost all of the Seller's package. Several positions together would hollow out the buyer's protection:

- The "all Claims of any nature" limitation language (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 and cl 12.3/13) would apply caps and time limits to fraud and title claims.
- Disclosure of the whole data room and public registers, combined with a blanket buyer-knowledge bar, would undercut most warranty claims.
- Bluefen, Riverlark and the bonuses are still open on the Seller's own Disclosure Letter.

The two fallbacks the Seller has adopted (20% cap and 18 months) each need Amelia Frost's prior written authority. None has been given, so neither is available.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1).
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The 20% figure is a conditional fallback that needs Amelia Frost's prior written authority for this draft, and none exists.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; only the excess above the basket is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; recovery from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, first-dollar.** The Seller's thresholds are five times ours and its deductible structure would remove up to AUD 250,000 from every recovery.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months. The Seller also wants any limitation to apply to all Claims "unless expressly stated otherwise".
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months after Completion for general Warranty Claims only.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given, and the default would quietly extend the general limits to other regimes.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime
- **Seller:** Title and capacity warranties take the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** A separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** Under the Seller's draft, a failure of title to the shares we are paying AUD 24m for would be capped at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month window.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** No express carve-out. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).
- **Buyer wants:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; insert an express overriding carve-out.** As drafted, the clause would purport to cap and time-bar fraud claims. This point is non-negotiable and no one can waive it.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2 generally disclose the entire data room (as at 5.00pm 22 Sep 2026), the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only, against identified warranties, with enough detail to assess the matter.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject 1.1 and 1.2 and accept only the specific disclosures (items 2–10) as drafted.** Disclosing the whole data room and public registers would let the Seller defeat claims on matters it never specifically identified.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Blanket bar on claims about anything known to the Buyer or its advisers, or discoverable from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** Delete the clause. Any qualifier should name the Seller's knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. Knowledge must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3.** Together with general disclosure, it would negate the warranties and could even defeat the specific indemnities we are negotiating for known issues.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied once the counterparty's written consent is delivered. Disclosure Letter item 2 confirms there is no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:** An effective consent, plus evidence that the DD-002 cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, as a Completion condition.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Make an effective consent with conditions satisfied a condition precedent, with a stronger endeavours standard.** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue, and a consent that is still conditional on delivery is not effective.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** A release "following Completion". Disclosure Letter item 3 confirms the roughly AUD 3.2m facility is unpaid and there is no discharge of security.
- **Buyer wants:** A current payout letter, repayment directly from Completion funds, and effective security releases delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** A post-completion release would need an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval, neither of which is offered. Without releases at Completion we would acquire encumbered assets despite the debt-free basis.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. The Seller is silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus any triggered on-costs shown as a specific funds-flow line item or otherwise seller-funded, such as a Debt-like deduction or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; require an express line item or seller funding including on-costs.** "A matter for the Seller" does not say who pays, and these obligations sit with the Company we are buying.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The cl 11.1 indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:** A broader IP indemnity covering ownership of and transfer failures in the SOW3 Project Materials. It should keep the SOW3 cure (cleared payment plus confirmatory assignment) and carry no assumption either way about the AUD 180,000.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; broaden the indemnity, keep the cure, and require evidence of cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment.** Under DD-004 cl 7.3 the risk is ownership of the IP, not just a fee. DD-010's AUD 180,000 is not independently verified, so we should neither assume it is owed nor assume it is paid.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material".
- **Buyer wants:** Logs preserved, the investigation continued, and regular updates to the Buyer before Completion, with appropriate warranty or indemnity protection pending the outcome.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the Seller's materiality characterisation and require preservation, investigation and update covenants.** On the current record there is no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or loss amount, so neither side should assume the matter is immaterial or serious. We should also avoid putting a dollar figure on it.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 total) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:** An assessment of each renewal from DD-008 and DD-011, read together, covering whether it is unavoidable or terminable, whether it is accrued, and whether it is genuinely ordinary course.
- **Recommendation:** **Accept neither label yet; reserve the position pending diligence.** The disclosure does not establish the character of the renewals, and our playbook rules out automatically classifying them as Debt or deducting them from the price.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 and cl 12.3/13). Tax and IP are folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories kept as separate regimes, with no general override.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Limit the limitation clauses to "general Warranty Claims" and preserve separate regimes expressly.** The catch-all wording is a hidden override that would collapse indemnities, covenants and fundamental claims into the general cap.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the DD-012 share register, and Disclosure Letter item 10 concedes the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence of ownership, absence of encumbrances and authority, such as ASIC records, PPSR searches, the issue and transfer history, constitution and shareholder arrangements, and board and shareholder authority.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject DD-012 as sufficient on its own and require independent evidence plus full title warranties under SPA-N-004.** DD-012 is an internal source supplied by the Seller and does not prove title.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** The Seller says tax and IP are "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP terms treated as open and not resolved, with no assumption of unlimited liability.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the claim that they are settled. Record these terms as open for negotiation as separate categories.** Nothing has been agreed, and accepting the Seller's framing would put Tax and IP under the 20% cap by default.

---

### Other points
- **Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009):** The disclosures describe a notification obligation and an assignment restriction, not a requirement for consent to the share sale. We should confirm the notification steps without assuming a consent condition is needed.
- **Disclosure Letter 1.4 (no admissions):** This is acceptable only if it cannot dilute specific indemnities or the Completion deliverables above.
- **Escalation:** No position here needs Amelia Frost's authority, provided we hold to our starting positions. If the team wants to consider the 20% cap, 18 months, or a post-completion Riverlark release, we need her written approval identifying this draft first.
